# Release Notes

## 0.44.0 - 2026-10-22 (deployed)

Production run `39742966975` deployed runtime SHA `9163a883822ce9def5acd884d653f948c56d5f91` on **2026-10-22**, with exact-main validation `39741869385` and normal production Environment approval. Readback passed at `2026-10-22T07:52:17.853142+00:00`. MINOR: a new backwards-compatible, purpose-bound paid-checkout browser-to-PWA authentication flow and POST `/billing/mono/open-app` public surface.

The paid bind/recovery return page offers **Відкрити застосунок / Open app** and, on explicit CSRF-protected submission, authenticates the checkout owner and redirects to exact `/app/`. The capability is signed, user/purpose-bound, expiring and single-use; the exact Monobank checkout must be PAID. GET does not authenticate; same-user replay is idempotent; an existing other-user session is never switched. Invalid, unpaid, failed, expired and used-token fresh-browser requests do not authenticate. Isolated local Chromium checkout acceptance and 244 regression tests passed for the unchanged runtime source. GitHub exact-main validation, built image artifact, deployment revision/readiness and verified encrypted off-host backup passed. Fresh production Chromium passed eight anonymous PWA/route guards; `python ops/readiness_smoke.py` exited 0.

**Acceptance boundary:** The artifact is deployed and revision/readiness readback passed. A real paid Monobank checkout -> authenticated production PWA journey was not exercised. The authenticated checkout scenarios were verified in isolated local Chromium, not against the live bank. Production probes were anonymous route/PWA guards; no provider call or financial write was requested, and production financial-row-count invariance was not independently measured. The earlier Telegram -> native Chrome owner-device acceptance gap remains open.

Documentation merge SHA is not the runtime SHA; this docs-only sync does not redeploy production. Older release-docs PR #74 is left untouched; this release does not claim that PR was merged.
